location: strip + picture + status bar: HDMI lost during a take
issue: No design for 'recording but no signal'. The recorder rejects no-signal frames while the take stays open, but the UI shows either REC or No signal, never both.
evidence: SourceRecordingAdapter.swift:59-63 (signalValid=false → reject()); states 1.3 Recording and 1.9 Waiting for HDMI are separate cards; no combined state on any page
scenario: Cable bumped mid-meeting: the strip still says Recording 00:31:44 while nothing is written for 40 s; the user trusts a backup with a hole in it.
recommendation: Add a combined state: strip 'REC · no signal 0:42 · not writing frames' (red text, counter keeps running), picture No-signal overlay keeps the REC pill, status bar error segment, attention dot. Define whether the take continues or splits when signal returns.
alternatives: Auto-pause the take on signal loss and resume on return (needs runtime change)
Split into a new take when signal returns

issue: The disk sequence stops at '2 min left: recording will stop when the drive is full'. The state at full (writer failure on every take on that drive, what was saved, whether Recover applies) is not designed.
evidence: states 4.5 and menubar g end at the warning; RecordingModel.swift:361-378 a failed flush throws writerFailure(lastError ?? 'Recording stopped after a source error.'); no disk-capacity check exists in code
scenario: Two feeds back up to 8TB; it fills at 1:42:10. Both strips show the generic source-error text, or nothing distinguishable, and the user doesn't know the takes were saved up to the last fragment.
recommendation: Design 'Stopped · drive full · saved to 1:41:58 (last fragment)' per strip, a single status-bar error naming the drive, the attention dot, and a recovery note if finalization failed. Map the writer error text to a plain 'drive full' message.
alternatives: Stop takes cleanly at ~1 min left, before the drive is actually full (needs runtime support; time-left is NEW)

location: effect chips / Processing switch while a consumer is live
issue: There is no transitional state for an effect or Processing change. The current app shows 'Applying change…' while pipelineEnabledApplied differs from the selection, and the producer drains and renegotiates format on effect changes. Round 3 dropped both the label and any warning.
evidence: FeedInterface.swift:431-444 AppliedPipelineState ('Applying change…'); README: 'The producer stops and drains its camera transport before negotiating a changed output format'; grep 'Applying' finds nothing in r3
scenario: Mid-call the user toggles Downscale on Feed 1; Zoom's picture blanks or reconnects and the UI gives no sign that this was expected or when it's done.
recommendation: Add 'Applying…' to the strip chips and result line, and an 'Output restarting' badge on the picture. Warn before format-changing toggles while a consumer is connected ('Zoom may briefly lose video').
alternatives: Defer format-changing toggles until the camera is not in use
Mark which effects are live-safe (LUT) vs format-changing (Downscale, Color, Frame rate)

issue: There's no 'saved' state. After Finishing, the Ready card resets the counter to 00:00:00. The current app keeps final take statistics visible until the next take, and that's the user's confirmation the backup exists.
evidence: README 'Final take statistics remain visible until the next take'; states 1.1 Ready shows 00:00:00; states 1.6 Failed keeps stats but no success equivalent
scenario: After a meeting the user stops recording and sees a zeroed strip: did it save? They must open Finder to check.
recommendation: Strip state 'Saved · 38:12 · 56.1 GB · Show in Finder' (collapsed: 'Saved 38:12'), kept until the next take; Record still enabled.
alternatives: Transient banner plus Recent Takes highlight

location: sidebar Output / onboarding step 1 during camera install
issue: The extension approval-pending state is missing. The installer moves through 'Requesting activation…' to 'Approve Ultracam in System Settings → … Camera Extensions', but round 3 only draws not-installed and installed.
evidence: ExtensionInstaller.swift:140-161 (pending, status strings); states 4.2/4.3 and the settings Camera pane have no pending or needs-approval visual
scenario: First launch: the user clicks Install Camera and nothing visible changes while macOS waits for approval; Zoom doesn't list Ultracam.
recommendation: Add Output states 'Requesting…' (spinner, buttons disabled) and 'Needs approval' (Open System Settings button). Echo them in the onboarding card, status bar and dropdown.

issue: 'Device gone' is not distinguished from 'no HDMI signal'. Only the first-run no-device card exists. The app reports 'Connect the UltraStudio and refresh inputs.' and disables Start when the selected device is missing, and a pull mid-take ends in a source error.
evidence: AppModel.swift:966 automatic status; canStartFeed requires a device; no device-removal handling in code (no matches); states 3.6 No HDMI signal assumes the device is present
scenario: The USB-C/Thunderbolt cable to the UltraStudio is unplugged: the UI says 'No HDMI signal, check the FX3', pointing at the wrong cable.
recommendation: Add a 'Device disconnected' state (picture + strip + attention dot) with Refresh, separate from no signal. Define the mid-take outcome (take finalized to last fragment).

location: green NEXT tally and dashed CUTTING
issue: NEXT has three definitions. Main pages show NEXT permanently on the non-air feed with 'cut after 10 s'. States uses NEXT for the director's queued cut and dashed CUTTING for a manual pending cut. Spec §5 defines NEXT as any queued cut (pending feed). The model only knows pendingCut/pendingCutTime (any queued cut) and pendingDirectorCut, with no predicted next feed when nothing is queued.
evidence: SwitcherCoordinator.swift:28-31,131-134; states 3.2/3.3; spec Picture tally table 'Next = Queued cut (pending feed)'; main-expanded Feed 2 NEXT with no pending cut
scenario: In a two-camera manual meeting Feed 2 always wears green NEXT, so green stops meaning anything. When a cut really is queued there's no visible change.
recommendation: One rule: no ring when nothing is queued; green NEXT only while pendingCut != nil (with the time from pendingCutTime). Drop the separate dashed state or keep it for manual cuts only, and drop predicted 'after 10 s' copy unless the director exposes it.
alternatives: Neutral 'Preview' outline for the idle non-air feed, broadcast-switcher style

location: Program when the on-air source stops or every source is unhealthy
issue: Two Program transitions are undesigned: stopping (or losing) the feed currently on air, and the evaluator's noHealthyFeed state, where Zoom ends up with black after 0.5 s.
evidence: SwitcherCoordinator.swift:6-11 SwitcherEvaluation.noHealthyFeed; AppModel.swift:929 setProgramSourceHealth(false); states 3.12 says only 'a stopped feed has no tally'
scenario: The on-air FX3 overheats and drops out. Does Program cut to Feed 2, hold the last frame or go black? The operator can't tell from the UI what Zoom now sees.
recommendation: Define and draw: (a) on-air source lost → automatic cut to a healthy source or 'Program: no source · Zoom receiving black' (red, status bar error, attention dot); (b) a warning when Stop Feed targets the on-air feed.

issue: Round 3 has nowhere to show automaticFeedStatus outside the dropdown. Its sub-states (preview-only demand, camera in use, restoring LUT, device missing, retry needed) have no window design. The old UI showed the status under the toggle.
evidence: AppModel.swift:958-967 (six status strings); sidebar Automation rows are bare switches; states 1.11 covers only failed start
scenario: With automatic mode on, the user opens the window and sees capture running with no camera app open; nothing says the visible preview is what's keeping it running.
recommendation: Add a status line under 'Start with camera apps' in the sidebar, mirrored in the strip header badge (e.g. 'Automatic · kept alive by preview').

location: toolbar Record All / Stop All control
issue: The primary record control is drawn only while recording (Stop All · 12:31 · N). Idle, disabled (no live feed or no folder), finishing, mixed paused and all-paused states are missing.
evidence: main-expanded/standalone/four-up toolbars all recording; menus show Record All disabled ('start a feed first') but the toolbar never does
scenario: Before a meeting the user looks for Record and the toolbar shows a red button with no label they've seen before.
recommendation: Draw all toolbar record states in states.html and spec §5, with labels: Record All / Stop All · 12:31 · 2 / Finishing… / Resume All when all are paused.

issue: There's no starting state anywhere. The capture path reports 'Opening UltraStudio…' and passes through Connecting, Waiting for HDMI and Ready before Live.
evidence: FeedInterface.swift:361-367 FeedStateLabel; AppModel.swift:685 'Opening UltraStudio…'
scenario: Pressing ⌘↩ shows nothing for a second; the user presses it again and stops the feed.
recommendation: Strip badge 'Starting…' with a spinner, picture placeholder 'Opening UltraStudio…', Start control disabled until established.

issue: Preview error with Retry preview (existing PreviewErrorNotice) and the 'insufficient presentation capacity' state for extra monitor windows are both absent from round 3.
evidence: FeedInterface.swift:119-136; README Monitor tools 'Additional windows can report insufficient presentation capacity'
scenario: The preview renderer fails: the picture stays black with no explanation, though camera output is fine.
recommendation: Picture overlay 'Preview failed · camera output continues · Retry Preview'; detached window 'Monitor unavailable · close another window'.

issue: The loading state ('Restoring your LUT…') is missing. Start is disabled while it runs and the effects are disabled.
evidence: AppModel canStartFeed (!loading); automaticFeedStatus 'Restoring your LUT…'; LUTControls 'Loading LUT…'
scenario: Launch, immediately ⌘↩: nothing happens and there's no reason given.
recommendation: Strip LUT chip spinner + 'Restoring LUT…'; Start disabled with tooltip.

location: menu bar icon and status bar precedence
issue: Icon states for paused, finishing and starting are undefined, as is precedence when recording and attention coincide. Stopped, automatic waiting, finishing, recording-failed and extension-pending status bar states aren't drawn either.
evidence: states 6.4 icon strip (6 states); states §5 status bar (5 states, 'worst wins' only for warning/error)
scenario: During a paused backup the icon still shows a red dot, so the user believes it's recording.
recommendation: Add a precedence table (error > attention > recording > paused > live > waiting > stopped) and draw paused (orange dot) and finishing.

issue: Neither the code nor the design handles system sleep during a live feed or recording.
evidence: no willSleep/didWake handling in Sources; no state on any page
scenario: A laptop lid closes mid-take: capture and the encoder stop abruptly and the take needs recovery; on wake nothing explains why.
recommendation: Runtime: hold a power assertion while recording or published (NEW). UI: 'Keeping your Mac awake while recording' in the status popover, plus a post-wake banner when a take was interrupted.

location: cut controls while a cut is pending or the target is skipped
issue: Only the picture shows pending or skipped state. The toolbar cut buttons, strip 'Cut to Feed N', sidebar camera rows and dropdown cut thumbnails have no pending or disabled-with-reason state.
evidence: states 3.3/3.5 picture-only; toolbar() and strip() builders have no pending branch
scenario: The user presses the toolbar Feed 2 button, sees no change for a frame-boundary wait, and presses again.
recommendation: Mirror pending (pulsing or dashed) and skipped (disabled with reason in the tooltip) on every cut control.

issue: Several key transitions are not specified: Recording→Finishing→Saved→Ready (what the strip shows at each step); Failed→new take (does the record button reuse the folder, keep the failed stats?); Automatic start failed→Retry→fails again (one attempt per session, then what?); disk low→full→stopped; no signal mid-take→signal returns (same take or new take?); bypass on→off while live (format renegotiation).
evidence: states captions describe single frames only; no transition notes in spec §5
scenario: Engineers implement each state differently because the in-between behavior is undefined.
recommendation: Add a transition table to spec §5: state → trigger → next state → what each component shows, with duration and cancellability.

issue: Effect changes renegotiate output format mid-meeting and no round-3 state warns or shows progress (see L10-03).
evidence: README format renegotiation; no 'Applying' state in r3
